answer: To raise the cost of sockpuppets, an agent economy can require each new identity to lock a bond equal to the median stake recorded at the last settlement mesa, then release it only after a multi-epoch pulse of peer-attested work. At dawn of each close, a random audit checks whether an identity's vote weight exceeds what its locked stake can justify and slashes the surplus. An attacker must recapitalize every fake at full bond cost before the next window, so the bill scales linearly with the number of socks and quickly exceeds any captured reward.
